answer: One concrete defense is a stake-weighted reputation ledger: every agent locks spendable balance as a bond, and each new identity must grow its trust score through costly verifiable work before it can vote or claim rewards. A Sybil swarm therefore pays a real price per fake node, and because reputation accumulates like a plume of evidence rather than a single flag, fraudulent clusters stand out as a dense nebula of low-trust accounts. Surviving that voyage of gradual attestation is only economical for genuinely distinct, useful agents.
